summary: The round-1 provenance-promotion bypass is resolved. A material relationship gap remains: admission groups checksum-identical aliases into one binding lineage, but private snapshots recognize only exact registration/media references. An admitted binding on an alias can therefore disappear from the original clip's snapshot, while creating a replacement binding is prohibited.

blocking_findings.description: Admission and snapshot collection disagree about registration identity. Register clip A, persist checksum-identical copies of its media and ingestion under new IDs, and store the first binding against those copied anchors. With no previous binding, admission accepts it. Snapshotting A then omits that binding because neither copied reference matches A's references. Attempting a binding on A's original anchors is subsequently rejected as a second lineage because the checksums match. Thus the sole admitted lineage for the original media is absent from its private snapshot/export. Executing the extracted admission and snapshot functions with field-only stand-ins reproduced omission and replacement rejection; the control using original anchors was included. This was a source-level reproduction, not a full repository execution.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Make snapshot reachability consistent with the original-registration identity enforced at admission, so an accepted alias binding cannot become unreachable from the corresponding selected clip. Add a repository/workspace regression where an alias receives the first binding, then verify snapshot/export inclusion of that binding and its pinned dependency closure while retaining unrelated-media exclusion.

claims_for_research.claim: Pydantic v2 BaseModel.model_copy(update=...) does not validate supplied update values.
RFC 3161 defines evidence that a datum existed before a particular time, requires a trustworthy time source, and does not examine the timestamped imprint beyond its length.
Local seal-plan-registration timestamps alone cannot prove generation followed intent sealing; witnessing intent existence does not itself witness generation.
Pydantic 2.13 changed RootModel shallow-copy behavior without adding validation of model_copy update values, with the cited release dated 2026-04-13.
RFC 9921, dated February 2026, standardizes COSE timestamp headers, distinguishes payload and signature timestamp semantics, and preserves the cited RFC 3161 properties.
SQLAlchemy 2.1 changes the default driver for postgresql:// URLs to psycopg 3, with the cited release dated 2026-09-24.
